question.prompt: The digits \(1,\) \(2,\) \(3,\) \(4,\) and \(9\) are each used once to form the smallest possible even five-digit number. The digit in the tens place is

solutions.explanation:
An even number must end in an even digit, so the last digit must be \(2\) or \(4\). For each ending, arrange the remaining digits in increasing order to make the number as small as possible. This works because, at the first place where two numbers differ, the smaller digit makes the smaller number.

If the last digit is \(2\), the smallest number is \(13492\). If the last digit is \(4\), the smallest number is \(12394\).

These cases cover every possible even ending. Since \(12394<13492\), the smallest allowed number is \(12394\). Its tens digit is \(9\), choice E.
solutions.title: Compare the possible even endings
